pr_body:
`dot_product` requires vectors to be unit-length. Previously, we would check that vectors were unit-length and throw if they were not. 

Instead, we will now auto-normalize vectors as they are indexed.

`cosine` will continue to behave as usual, not normalizing the vectors.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/98935
pr_title: Auto-normalize dot_product vectors at index & query
pr_comment: Hi @benwtrent, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

PR: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/98946 fixes many of the failing tests. There are multiple tests assuming `index: false` and now they have to specifically set it.

One of the difficulties is v7RestCompatibility. 

If we:
 - index: true
 - dot_product == auto-normalize

The v7RestCompatability tests will fail. Because those tests do not specify `index: false`, mainly because that option didn't exist in v7.

For non-indexed vectors the behavior is exactly the same. But the combination of indexing by default and choosing dot_product breaks those tests.

Do we want to keep the default as `cosine` without auto-normalization? 

Do we think this is truly a breaking restcompat change?
For now, I will remove the default to `dot_product` part of this change. We will have to discuss that further.
